articles.title: San Diego State football program dealing with mumps outbreak ahead of first-ever Pac-12 game
articles.summary: San Diego County announced Wednesday night that there had been 14 confirmed mumps cases at SDSU.
articles.body:
Numerous San Diego State football players have the mumps.

San Diego County announced Wednesday that there had been 14 confirmed cases and one probable case of the mumps at the university. In a statement distributed to the school, the university said "the outbreak remains within a single athletic team, and one associated case."

The number of mumps cases is up significantly from Sept. 18, when SDSU officially announced three confirmed cases and two probable cases of mumps within that sports team.

At his news conference earlier in the week, SDSU coach Sean Lewis alluded to players dealing with non-football injuries and sicknesses but would not go into detail or identify any of the players.

"Not going to comment any further about all of that out of respect for those kids' privacy and what we have — and what they're doing," Lewis said.

Wednesday evening, San Diego State had 15 players either listed as "out" or "doubtful" for Saturday's game against Texas State on its initial Pac-12 injury report.

That group of players included top running backs Javian Kinnard and Lucky Sutton. Kinnard, who is among those doubtful, has 56 carries for 312 yards. Sutton, who is listed as out, has 45 carries for 150 yards and three scores. Both players suffered injuries in the team's Week 4 loss to Toledo.

Mumps is a viral illness that can cause painful swelling of the salivary glands and make it difficult to eat and talk. The virus can also make people develop flu-like symptoms and, in some cases, lead to swollen testicles in men.

The respiratory virus can easily spread among those who are in close contact and the typical treatment is to let it run its course over the course of a week or so. The school is providing a free vaccination clinic on Thursday for students who want to get a booster shot because of the ongoing outbreak.

San Diego State is 1-3 entering its first Pac-12 game ever against the Bobcats in Week 5. The Aztecs have lost all three games they have played to FBS teams by at least 13 points so far this season as they moved from the Mountain West in the offseason. The rebuilt Pac-12 added SDSU, Texas State, Fresno State, Colorado State, Boise State and Utah State to form an eight-team conference with Oregon State and Washington State after the league essentially disbanded ahead of the 2024 season.

articles.title: Week 5 college football viewer's guide: Ohio State's trip to Iowa headlines the first weekend of October
articles.summary: Week 5 features three matchups between ranked teams.
articles.body:
The first weekend of the second month of the regular season has three matchups between ranked teams and a host of other intriguing games. Let's get to it.

No. 7 Alabama at No. 16 Mississippi State

We could learn a lot about both the Crimson Tide and the Bulldogs on Saturday.

Mississippi State is 4-0 in back-to-back seasons for the first time since World War II. Last year, the Bulldogs finished the regular season 5-7 before earning a bowl birth because there weren't enough six-win teams. MSU lost that game too and finished 5-8.

It's hard to see how eight losses is in play this season for Mississippi State. Especially with the way that Kamario Taylor has started the season. He's the No. 3 Heisman favorite and has already thrown for 14 touchdowns while also showing plenty of ability to escape the pocket and get first downs with his legs.

He's gotten support from RB Fluff Bothwell, who has rushed for 402 yards and three scores, and WR Anthony Evans III has 28 catches for 408 yards. The Bulldogs' offense is averaging 7.5 yards a play and is by far the best unit Alabama has faced so far this season.

However, the same thing can be said for Alabama's offense against the Mississippi State defense. The Tide are a completely different team with Keelon Russell at quarterback, as he's helped unlock the Alabama run game. The Tide are rushing the ball nearly 40 times a game for almost 5 yards a carry. Opponents have scored just one rushing touchdown against MSU all season. Alabama should at least match that.

The Tide have also been very good at forcing turnovers. Opponents have turned the ball over 12 times in Alabama's four games. Mississippi State has just three turnovers all season.

Iowa's last-second win over Michigan in Week 4 was so big that it brought ESPN's "College GameDay" to town for the first time in two decades. The win also gives us the only matchup between top 15 teams this weekend after the Hawkeyes moved up three spots in the AP Top 25.

Will Kirk Ferentz be more aggressive against an offense that is far better than Michigan's? The game-winning TD pass last week overshadowed a typically conservative decision from the longtime Iowa coach. Trailing 19-14, Iowa opted for a 51-yard field goal attempt facing a fourth-and-6 with less than three minutes to go. Yes, a made kick in that scenario would have meant Iowa only needed a field goal on its final drive for the win — but it also would've required the Hawkeyes to get a stop of Michigan's offense.

Ohio State is averaging 45 points and 7.8 yards a play this season. WR Jeremiah Smith is basically uncoverable and Bo and Ja'Kobi Jackson are combining to average over 6 yards a carry. Iowa has the best scoring defense in the country at eight points a game and is allowing just 4.1 yards per play. But it won't be able to win this game on its own. Iowa QB Hank Brown will need to be even better than he was against Michigan. The Auburn transfer was 21-of-35 for 227 yards and two scores against the Wolverines.

This is a matchup of ranked teams because voters apparently couldn't find another team they liked for the final spot in the AP Top 25 after Missouri's loss to Mississippi State. That loss was the 20th of coach Eli Drinkwitz's tenure against a ranked opponent. Missouri has won just eight games against ranked teams in that timeframe.

A ninth won't qualify as a major upset according to the betting line, and it'll go a long way to showing that Missouri has the path to an eight or even nine-win season with a schedule that still includes No. 9 Ole Miss, No. 1 Texas and No. 2 Georgia. A loss — especially a bad one — and Missouri fans are going to wonder if a bowl game is even in the cards.

The explosive Florida run game with Jadan Baugh has been what Missouri's was a year ago with Ahmad Hardy . There's still no timetable for the Tigers star's return to the field and the run game has suffered without him. QB Austin Simmons has completed 66% of his passes for 947 yards and 11 TDs, but Cayden Lee and Donovan Olugbode have caught 47 of 79 completions.

The Gators showed in their win against Ole Miss how they can pay when opposing defenses focus too much on stopping the run. QB Aaron Philo is averaging 10.5 yards an attempt and completing 72% of his passes. Missouri's pass defense has given up its share of big plays this year and Florida could be well-positioned to capitalize.

TCU quarterback Jaden Craig said this week that the Horned Frogs held a players-only meeting on Monday after a road loss to a UCF team that started a backup quarterback.

TCU is 2-2 this season despite not allowing more than 21 points in a game. The Horned Frogs turned the ball over four times against the Knights as Craig threw two interceptions and receiver Ed Small had two fumbles. TCU's defense has shown that it can keep the Horned Frogs in games. Can the offense avoid the mistakes that have plagued them against North Carolina and UCF?

BYU is coming off a bye week and again has one of the more dominant rushing attacks in the country (in a limited sample size). The Cougars are averaging 6.7 yards a carry and nearly 263 yards a game and have been able to keep LJ Martin fresh, too. Martin has carried the ball just 42 times for 328 yards this season. Twenty of those carries came in a 28-17 win over Arizona in Week 2 and he had 15 carries for 176 yards and three touchdowns against Colorado State two weeks ago.

The Tigers can do a lot of making up for a Week 1 loss to LSU with an upset win against the Hurricanes. Or, a similar result will be further proof of just how far Clemson has fallen from being a perennial contender.

Such is the reactionary world of college football, and this is a Clemson team that's willing to lean into the run game with freshman QB Tait Reynolds now starting. But it seems unlikely that what worked at Cal in Week 4 will work against Miami.

Reynolds was 14-of-22 passing for 106 yards and an interception against the Bears. That can be OK when you rush for 257 yards and two scores against an inferior opponent. But the Miami offense is an absolute juggernaut. There's a reason this line favors Miami by more than two touchdowns.

The Hurricanes are averaging 8.5 yards a play and 589 yards a game so far this season. It's comical how good Miami's offense has been — and it's a statement that is still true without counting a 77-7 win over Florida A&M.

Miami could really exploit Clemson on the ground. The Tigers have held Georgia Southern and Cal to 108 combined rushing yards … while giving up 309 rushing yards to LSU and 214 to North Carolina. Mark Fletcher Jr. and Javian Mallory could have big days.

Pitt at Virginia Tech (-3.5) (7 p.m. ET Friday, ESPN): The winner of this game better be ranked. Both teams are 4-0 and 1-0 in ACC play. Pitt QB Mason Heintschel has thrown for 13 TDs after a seven-TD performance earlier in the year, while Virginia Tech's Ethan Grunkemeyer is 101-of-136 for 1,012 yards and eight touchdowns.

No. 3 Notre Dame (-21) at North Carolina (Noon ET, ESPN): Yes, the line is massive. But it's another chance to see just how far North Carolina has progressed in Year 2 under Bill Belichick. Especially after an off week. Will the Tar Heels be able to slow down CJ Carr ? Opposing QBs have thrown for fewer than 190 yards per game and just one touchdown against UNC this season.

Auburn at No. 17 Tennessee (-7.5) (3:30 p.m. ET, ESPN): This could be the first big win for Alex Golesh at Auburn, while Tennessee aims to bounce back from its loss to Texas. It's also the first of four straight games against ranked opponents for the Tigers. After Tennessee, Auburn has No. 2 Georgia, No. 11 LSU and No. 9 Ole Miss to close out October.

Virginia (-2.5) at Florida State (3:30 p.m. ET, ESPN2): The Seminoles are home underdogs for the second straight ACC game. That shows you where things are in Tallahassee. A loss drops FSU to 2-3 with games against Louisville , Miami and Clemson coming up.

No. 24 Kentucky at South Carolina (-3) (4:15 p.m. ET, SEC Network): This is another home team that badly needs a conference win. The Gamecocks will be without edge rusher Dylan Stewart as he serves his one-game suspension for throwing a punch at Alabama's Josh Ford. A win for the Wildcats would be the team's first 2-0 start in SEC play since 2023.

articles.title: North Macedonia v Scotland: Key Nations League questions for Sebastien Pocognoli
articles.summary: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli has decisions to make as he searches for his first win in North Macedonia on Saturday.
articles.body:
Nations League: North Macedonia v Scotland

Two games, one point, no goals. And a home debut hampered by an early red card.

New Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli might have hoped to know more about his side by now. But little was learned at Hampden on Tuesday as his 10-man team were outclassed by Switzerland.

That makes Saturday’s match in North Macedonia - live on the BBC - even more important. A first win under the Belgian is needed.

How might Scotland achieve that? And what are the key questions facing the head coach?

You are the Scotland boss - what would you do?

New coach, new players, but same old failings hamper Scotland

Hampden debut to forget but Pocognoli looks at bigger picture

Goalkeeper Angus Gunn admitted he'd "probably be disappointed" when he looked back at the goals he conceded against the Swiss.

The 30-year-old was Steve Clarke's number one at the World Cup and, since then, has remained in the United States with San Jose Earthquakes.

But a far from successful start at his new club - where he has conceded 23 goals in 11 games - has continued into international duty.

Ricardo Rodriguez's opener was, in pundit Andy Halliday's view, "shoulder height [with] not a lot of pace". Gunn's failure to keep it out was "so poor", he said.

While there was little that could be done for the Swiss' deserved second, the goalkeeper didn't cover himself in glory for the third goal, with Zeki Amdouni's finish going through him.

Gunn's far from convincing performance sparked a conversation around whether he should start on Saturday.

Will Pocognoli change goalkeeper after Swiss loss?

In truth, he probably will due to the lack of better options.

Scott Bain is in the Scottish Premiership with Falkirk, while Jon McCracken is with Bradford in England's League One. Liam Kelly is yet to be anywhere other than the bench for Rangers this term.

But Pocognoli has not shied away from big calls so far - his initial bold squad and his offering of three debuts in two games stand out. It wouldn't be out of the question for him to shake things up in Skopje.

"They were good strikes, but as a goalkeeper, I'm always disappointed when I concede a goal," Gunn acknowledged after facing the Swiss. "I'll look back and see what I could have done better and get better for the next game."

Who knows when that next game will be...

While there is a little uncertainty in goal, Pocognoli may have been given a bit of clarity about the make-up of his defence in his first two games.

Substitute Stephen Welsh was a winner on a grim night against the Swiss.

The Swansea City defender settled nicely into his debut in Slovenia on Saturday on the left side of the back three, and might have felt aggrieved to drop to the bench on Tuesday as the head coach handed a debut to Luis Binks.

But Jack Hendry's red card necessitated a reshuffle and Welsh was restored to the team in a more familiar position on the right and performed admirably again.

Not only is the former Celtic and Motherwell defender vocal and versatile, he is also comfortable carrying the ball - a key asset in Pocognoli's style.

His unexpected home debut ought to help him back into the starting line-up on Saturday, especially with Hendry suspended.

While the second half in Slovenia showed Pocognoli's system can be exciting, it remains unclear if it best suits this Scotland squad?

Two games in and winger Ben Gannon-Doak has yet to start. His impact as a substitute in both has been notable, leading Halliday to say he'd be "shocked" if the Bournemouth player didn't start against Group B1's bottom side.

However, in the Belgian's 3-4-1-2 set-up, there is no obvious place for him. Wing-back would seem the most likely, but the 20-year-old's defensive instincts are not the same as those of Aaron Hickey or Nathan Patterson.

Perhaps Pocognoli needs to be more flexible - something he said he is but has yet to show in his shape. But if he wants to stick to his preference, is this the game to try Gannon-Doak at wing-back?

Gannon-Doak offers an attacking threat like few others do in a Scotland shirt. He could do with a hand from some pals. John McGinn, anyone?

The Aston Villa captain won a bounty of fouls against the Swiss, and though he was much-improved like the rest in the second half at the Stozice Arena, he's still not reaching the levels he does at his Premier League club.

Pocognoli needs more from the Tartan Army talisman as he hurtles towards a century of caps - he's on 91.

The vice-captain is another whose name has been mentioned in the 'does this system suit Scotland' conversation.

It's been a while since McGinn delivered one of those big performances for his country, but his ability to create a moment of magic and drive a team forward makes him difficult to drop.

Another big call for Pocognoli to ponder...

What should be a little more straightforward is giving Kieron Bowie another start.

The Sassuolo striker was sacrificed just over 10 minutes into his first Scotland start to make space for Welsh in defence.

His partnership with Oli McBurnie showed promising signs in the 20 minutes or so they were together in Slovenia, but there was little time to build on that cameo against the Swiss. Surely he and the Hull City striker will get another chance?

If there were any concerns McBurnie wasn't up for the fight - five years on from his last international involvement - they have been quashed in these past two games.

His work-rate as a largely solo striker - hauling his team up and holding the ball in - was commendable. If only Bowie was still on the field for the flurry of flick-ons he won in the first half.

Pocognoli has inherited one of the overriding problems Clarke wrestled with during his spell - scoring goals. That’s four games now without one, and the Scots are just 25 minutes away from setting a new - unwanted - record for failing to score.

In 1970-71, they went 447 minutes without finding the back of the net - it’s been 422 minutes of football since McGinn’s deflected strike against Haiti in Boston.

articles.title: El Athletic abrirá Lezama el próximo martes
articles.standfirst: Los rojiblancos entrenarán a puerta abierta el 6 de octubre
articles.summary: Los rojiblancos entrenarán a puerta abierta el 6 de octubre
articles.body: El Athletic ha anunciado este jueves que la próxima semana brindará a sus aficionados la posibilidad de ver en acción a los rojiblancos en Lezama. Los leones se entrenarán a puerta abierta el martes 6 de octubre en una sesión que arrancará a las 11:00. La última sesión a puerta abierta generó malestar en la afición rojiblanca ya que únicamente pudieron acceder a dicha sesión los socios y miembros del Club Athletic. En esta ocasión estos tendrán prioridad para reservar su entrada de manera gratuita hasta completar el aforo. Cada socio o miembro del Club Athletic podrá obtener dos invitaciones. En caso de que durante este jueves y la mañana del viernes el aforo no se completase, a partir de las 13:30 del mismo viernes cualquier persona podrá conseguir una invitación unicamente utilizando su cuenta digital Athleticzale gratuita.

articles.title: Denis y Aleñá para tapar el agujero de la medular
articles.standfirst: Nadie se ha adueñado de la tercera posición del centro del campo tras la grave lesión de Mikel Rodríguez.
articles.summary: Nadie se ha adueñado de la tercera posición del centro del campo tras la grave lesión de Mikel Rodríguez.
articles.body: El gran inicio de curso del Alavés ha permitido a Quique Sánchez Flores mover pocas piezas de un partido a otro. Cuando algo funciona es mejor tocar lo menos posible y el técnico madrileño lo está cumpliendo, aunque hay una posición en el centro del campo que no tiene dueño desde la grave lesión de Mikel Rodríguez y hasta tres futbolistas diferentes han desfilado por esa zona en las últimas cuatro jornadas. El centrocampista de Getaria se había asentado al lado de Antonio Blanco y Pablo Ibáñez en la sala de máquinas tras ser una de las sensaciones babazorras en las primeras jornadas. Sin embargo, la rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior de la pierna derecha que sufrió en un entrenamiento le sacó de una ecuación que ahora tiene otra incógnita por resolver. Carles Aleñá, Denis Suárez y Protesoni han sido los jugadores que han ocupado esa posición en el último mes de competición. El uruguayo lo hizo en San Mamés en un rol muy diferente y con Pablo Ibáñez ganando más altura, pero en condiciones normales, el sustituto de Rodríguez en la sala de máquinas debe partir de la pugna que mantienen Aleñá y Denis. De momento, el gallego ha sido titular en dos partidos y el catalán en uno. Denis ha cogido cierta ventaja para acompañar a Blanco e Ibáñez en la medular, aunque necesita más continuidad para rendir a su mejor versión. En Santander dejó buenos momentos de juego en la segunda mitad, pero todavía no ha alcanzada la versión que ofreció en algunas fases del pasado curso con Coudet. Por su parte, Aleñá busca recuperar el protagonismo que perdió desde la llegada de Quique, con quien sólo ha sido titular en 5 partidos de 17 posibles. "Mikel nos ha dejado el listón altísimo y sabemos que todo aquel que quiera jugar en esa posición tiene que alcanzar ese nivel", advertía Quique cuatro días después del grave contratiempo sufrido por el centrocampista. Del rendimiento de Aleña y Denis dependerán los planes del Alavés de cara a buscar reforzar esa posición en el mercado invernal. Rodríguez ofreció un gran rendimiento en las primeras jornadas y ahora es responsabilidad de ellos llenar el vacío que ha dejado su lesión.

articles.title: Así hacía trampa el City: empresas 'tapadera', pago a través de terceros y palancas ficticias
articles.standfirst: El informe de 40 páginas de la Premier detalla con ejemplos la ingeniería financiera que permitió encubrir gastos extra durante una década para hacer crecer al club, que insiste en su inocencia
articles.summary: El informe de 40 páginas de la Premier detalla con ejemplos la ingeniería financiera que permitió encubrir gastos extra durante una década para hacer crecer al club, que insiste en su inocencia
articles.body: Hasta en ocho ocasiones se usa la palabra "sham" (farsa) en el durísimo informe de la Comisión Independiente de la Premier contra el Manchester City. En las 40 páginas, muchos nombres, de testigos y cargos, se omiten, por ahora. El equipo inglés, acusado de 114 cargos financieros y de falsear sus cuentas a propósito, engañando a la competición y a sus rivales, al fútbol, responde que es inocente. Incluso, según su CEO, Ferran Soriano, que "todo es una conspiración". Abu Dhabi United Group, dueños del City desde hace 18 años, entendió desde el principio que la única vía para instalar a un equipo medio, en la élite, era engordando sus cuentas por patrocinio, real o inflado, tal y como explica la BBC, ya que la UEFA como la Premier League estaban a punto de introducir normas de juego limpio financiero allá por 2010. Y durante casi una década, el denominado Plan de Financiación Encubierta logró ocultar aproximadamente 1.000 millones de euros, en financiación por patrocinio, básicamente porque eran los dueños y no los sponsors, los que pagaban la mayor parte del patrocinio o incluso parte de los sueldos de los jugadores. Desde 2010 el City partió los acuerdos de patrocinio entre una tarifa base, que era la que de verdad pagaban los patrocinadores, y una tarifa adicional, que aportaban los nuevos y adinerados dueños... lo que les permitiría, entre otras cosas, invertir en jugadores prohibitivos. Según la Premier "dio la impresión engañosa a terceros (incluidos los reguladores y sus auditores) de que sus ingresos comerciales provenientes de acuerdos de patrocinio eran mucho, mucho mayores de lo que realmente eran y de vez en cuando lo modificaban para facilitar el ocultamiento continuo y evitar preguntas difíciles". En algunos casos, estas palancas llegaron a ser hasta de 125 millones como en 2017: de los 11 declarados a los 134 reales. En total se estima que los patrocinadores pagaron 119,25 millones en esos nueve años investigados, pero que el City los infló como si ingresaran 1111 millones, casi diez veces más. Vamos con un par de ejemplos prácticos, extraídos de declaraciones de testigos realizadas en privado durante la investigación: 1. Se utilizó una empresa tapadera como Fordham (envuelta en otras actividades legales bajo el nombre de Proyecto Longbow) para que adquiriera del club (a un precio muy inflado) los derechos de imagen de sus jugadores. Se ocultaba así de nuevo el verdadero origen del dinero para ingresar más fondos como ingresos operativos. Así entraron unos 30 millones y se excluyeron de los gastos otros 55, 'todo erróneamente', pero con el "conocimiento y aprobación del club", según el fallo judicial. 2. Otro ejemplo: los contratos millonarios de jugadores y entrenadores se ocultaban de las cuentas, con el pago de salarios a través de terceros que, una vez más, los realizaban los propios dueños. Existen tres casos distintos relacionados con este asunto, cuyos nombres han sido omitidos en el documento... de momento. Y el montante final roza los 20 millones. Esto "quedó registrado en un contrato de consultoría" y "ocultó el verdadero alcance de las responsabilidades del club", dice el informe. El club tiene derecho a apelar las conclusiones de la Comisión independiente y dispone de hasta el viernes 2 de octubre para ejercer ese derecho. La intención de la Junta Directiva de la Premier League es que todo el proceso (incluidas las apelaciones y la publicación de las decisiones pertinentes) concluya lo antes posible.

articles.title: La UEFA confirma que ya tiene el informe del Madrid del caso Negreira
articles.standfirst: El organismo comunica que analizará "la cantidad sustancial de documentos" recibidos del club blanco para continuar con el expediente que se abrió en 2023
articles.summary: El organismo comunica que analizará "la cantidad sustancial de documentos" recibidos del club blanco para continuar con el expediente que se abrió en 2023
articles.body: "La UEFA confirma haber recibido del Real Madrid CF una cantidad sustancial de documentos relacionados con la investigación en curso sobre el FC Barcelona en el caso de José María Enríquez Negreira, exvicepresidente del Comité Técnico de Árbitros de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (el denominado «caso Negreira»). Este es el comunicado que el máximo organismo del fútbol europeo ha trasladado a través de sus canales oficiales. "Los inspectores de ética y disciplina de la UEFA también han recibido estos documentos, que analizarán en el marco de su revisión", añade el comunicado. El Madrid ya tenía preparado hace meses un extenso informe con todo el expediente del caso Negreira y lleva tiempo intentando que el Barça pague las consecuencias a nivel internacional una vez que en el ámbito nacional no hay excesivos avances. La previsión es que la instrucción se cierre a final de 2026 y se señale el juicio para el próximo una vez que la jueza encargada del caso rechazó la solicitud del Real Madrid (apoyada por la Fiscalía) para prorrogar la investigación otros seis meses más. Pero el Madrid ha hecho las paces con la UEFA y está a punto de hacerlo con la EFC, la asociación de clubes europeos, y ha insistido en todas las conversaciones en la necesidad de un castigo al club azulgrana por el bien del fútbol y la credibilidad de este deporte. Ahora la pelota está en el tejado de la UEFA, que tiene que valorar ahora si es motivo de sanción una vez que se estudien los documentos del Madrid y las alegaciones que probablemente presentará el Barcelona. Los Inspectores de Ética y Disciplina de la UEFA abrieron en marzo 2023 el expediente de este caso al detectar indicios de una posible violación de su marco legal debido a los pagos realizados a José María Enríquez Negreira, pero decidió dejar el expediente en suspenso de forma provisional a la espera de que avanzara la vía penal en la justicia ordinaria española. El Madrid se volcó de lleno sobre el caso Negreira una vez que el Barça le dejó solo por la Superliga. El pasado 17 de junio, el club anunció en un comunicado que había enviado a la UEFA un escrito para poner "en conocimiento de la UEFA la existencia de evidencias relevantes que refuerzan de forma concluyente los indicios ya conocidos desde el inicio sobre la existencia de pagos prolongados en el tiempo, opacos y carentes de cualquier justificación verificable" del Barça por el caso Negreira. "El Real Madrid subraya que estos hechos configuran, desde la perspectiva del derecho disciplinario deportivo, un riesgo sistémico de máxima gravedad para la integridad de las competiciones, al evidenciar la existencia de una estructura de influencia indebida sobre el estamento arbitral, incompatible con los principios esenciales de igualdad competitiva, neutralidad, imparcialidad e imprevisibilidad del resultado deportivo", añadió dicho comunicado, en el que instaba a la UEFA a la reanudación inmediata del expediente disciplinario incoado en su día por la UEFA, considerando inaceptable que esta situación se haya prolongado en el tiempo, ya que su persistencia compromete seriamente la credibilidad del fútbol, de sus instituciones y de sus dirigentes, por lo que exige una respuesta firme, ejemplar e inmediata en el ámbito deportivo, independiente del devenir de los procedimientos judiciales en curso".

articles.title: Stephen King: How horror writer is keeping Highland League side Buckie Thistle going
articles.summary: Buckie Thistle thank famous horror writer Stephen King for his "fantastic" donation towards a fundraising campaign aimed at securing the future of the club.
articles.body:
Buckie Thistle have thanked famous horror writer Stephen King for his "fantastic" donation towards a fundraising campaign aimed at securing the future of the club.

The pair struck up a relationship six years ago when King featured the Highland League club in his book, If It Bleeds.

At the time, the best-selling writer of works including Carrie and The Shining donated two copies of the novel to the Moray side, one of which was auctioned off.

The 79-year-old has helped boost their coffers again this time round as the club tries to navigate its way out of its current financial predicament.

Buckie Thistle interim president Daniel Farquhar told BBC Scotland: "It is fantastic. We reached out and we are just really grateful for Stephen to take the time to donate something.

"We don't want to disclose the sum but it is a nice little figure that will keep us going. It will help pay for players and operation costs and things like that.

"The response we got back in the email from him was 'hopefully this donation inspires others to get involved and put their hands in their pockets as well', so we are eternally grateful and we just hope it does inspire others to help us."

Buckie Thistle found themselves in the spotlight in early 2024 when they played Celtic in the Scottish Cup, losing 5-0 in Glasgow.

The Highland Jags have found it tough to make ends meet after long-standing president Garry Farquhar stepped down for health reasons earlier this year.

His son Daniel said: "Our operating costs of around £20,000 per month are far outweighing the money coming in at the moment, so we are undergoing a big task just now just to look at expenditure, try and reduce that.

"We have had in the region of £55,000 worth of donations in the last five or six weeks, so it is phenomenal."

articles.title: Paul Raynor: Bristol Rovers assistant reveals bowel cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Bristol Rovers assistant head coach Paul Raynor reveals he has been diagnosed with bowel cancer.
articles.body:
Bristol Rovers assistant head coach Paul Raynor has been diagnosed with bowel cancer.

The 60-year-old said doctors had found a tumour and he would undergo chemotherapy and radiotherapy, starting later this month.

Raynor added that the cancer had not spread to any major organs which was a "massive positive" and he had been told the chances of success were high.

"We're going to try and beat this," Raynor told the club website. , external

"We will beat this and then be back on the grass helping the guys later in the season with a bit of luck.

"The plan is I'm going to be here as much as possible. I'm going to be there on matchdays, and I aim to be and I want to be. If I'm well enough, I certainly will be."

Raynor joined Rovers boss Steve Evans at the Memorial Stadium in December 2025, helping them to avoid relegation to the National League and they are among the favourites for promotion from League Two this season.

He said the cancer had been discovered after he submitted a sample.

"I was a typical man and left it, with my wife badgering me into doing it," Raynor added.

"So I did it and a week later I was told there was an abnormal reading, and I had to go in for a full check. Within an hour, I was sat with a consultant and being told they had found a tumour."

Pre-match, post-match and topical Pirates content

Raynor has worked with Evans at nine different clubs, first at Boston United and then including Crawley Town, Rotherham United, Leeds United and Stevenage.

"I've known and worked with the gaffer for 25 years and he's a massive friend and these last few weeks he's been absolutely immense but everyone has," Raynor added.

"If it wasn't for my good lady Karen I wouldn't have sent the sample off and it could've been too late and the ramifications could be anything. They're telling me there's a good chance it's curable but if I hadn't done that sample it could've been a lot, lot worse.

"The message is, get your samples done, whatever tests you need go and get it done because it's massively important."

articles.standfirst: El delantero publicó en redes unas fotos con la Bota de Oro y el Balón de Bronce del Mundial, apenas tres días después de cerrarse las votaciones del Balón de Oro, que se entrega el 26 de octubre
articles.summary: El delantero publicó en redes unas fotos con la Bota de Oro y el Balón de Bronce del Mundial, apenas tres días después de cerrarse las votaciones del Balón de Oro, que se entrega el 26 de octubre
articles.body: Kylian Mbappé sigue optando por reivindicarse. El delantero del Real Madrid publicó este jueves en sus redes sociales una serie de fotografías mostrando la Bota de Oro y el Balón de Bronce que conquistó en el pasado Mundial, los galardones que lo reconocieron como máximo goleador y tercer mejor jugador del torneo. Y es que el gesto del francés no es casual. Las votaciones del Balón de Oro se cerraron hace apenas tres días, y la gala que coronará al mejor futbolista del año está programada para el próximo 26 de octubre. Mbappé, uno de los grandes candidatos junto a Lamine Yamal, Harry Kane y el vigente ganador, Ousmane Dembélé, aprovecha así cualquier escaparate para recordar sus méritos de una temporada en la que lideró a su selección y, cuando las lesiones se lo permitieron, al Madrid. El propio delantero ha protagonizado una intensa campaña en las últimas semanas. En declaraciones a France Football, la publicación que organiza el premio, se mostró convencido de que este "es un buen año para ganarlo", y zanjó los rumores de tensión con Dembélé: "Ya he hablado con él, no hay ningún problema, es un amigo". A su favor ha remado también Thibaut Courtois, que pidió públicamente el galardón para su compañero en una entrevista reciente. No todo han sido buenas noticias, eso sí. Mbappé regresó tocado del último parón de selecciones, y los Servicios Médicos del Real Madrid le diagnosticaron una hiperextensión de la cápsula posterior de la rodilla izquierda, una dolencia que el club dejó pendiente de evolución.

articles.title: Comunicado del Madrid sobre el caso Negreira: "El Real Madrid pide a la UEFA que la investigación avance con la máxima celeridad"
articles.standfirst: El club blanco envió un amplio dossier a la UEFA denunciando el caso
articles.summary: El club blanco envió un amplio dossier a la UEFA denunciando el caso
articles.body: Pocos minutos después de que UEFA emitiera un comunicado asegurando que había recibido toda la documentación sobre el 'Caso Negreira' por parte del Real Madrid, el club blanco hizo un escrito pidiendo a la UEFA que actúe con la máxima celeridad en este caso. Un comunicado contundente por parte del Madrid en el que asegura que ha aportado "evidencias sobre unos hechos de extraordinaria gravedad, que afectan directamente a la integridad de la competición y a la confianza en el sistema arbitral". "Ante la comunicación realizada en el día de hoy por UEFA en relación con el denominado “caso Negreira”, el Real Madrid C. F. manifiesta lo siguiente: UEFA ha confirmado la recepción de la denuncia presentada por el Real Madrid C. F. y la continuación de la investigación relativa a los pagos efectuados durante las dos últimas décadas por el F. C. Barcelona a quien fuera vicepresidente del Comité Técnico de Árbitros. La denuncia presentada por nuestro club incorpora abundante documentación y evidencias sobre unos hechos de extraordinaria gravedad, que afectan directamente a la integridad de la competición y a la confianza en el sistema arbitral. El Real Madrid C. F. considera imprescindible que, una vez que UEFA dispone de esta documentación, la investigación avance con la máxima celeridad hasta su completa conclusión y que los órganos competentes adopten las decisiones que correspondan conforme a la gravedad de los hechos acreditados. Nuestro club continuará colaborando activamente con UEFA y ejerciendo cuantas actuaciones estén a su alcance para el esclarecimiento de unos hechos que considera incompatibles con los principios de integridad, transparencia y juego limpio que deben presidir el fútbol europeo". El club blanco, en su comunicado, pide a la UEFA que actúe con "máxima celeridad" en su investigación para zanjar un asunto que estalló públicamente el 15 de febrero de 2023 y que en España aún se encuentra en investigación bajo la justicia. El Madrid reitera que se trata de un asunto de extrema gravedad e insiste a la UEFA a que llegue hasta el final del caso. El amplio dossier aportado por el Real Madrid está ya en manos de la UEFA y el club blanco confía en que el máximo organismo del fútbol europeo actúe sobre unos hechos que "considera incompatibles con los principios de integridad, transparencia y juego limpio que deben presidir el fútbol europeo".

articles.title: El órdago de José Riestra: “Si el Sporting no asciende, nos vamos”
articles.standfirst: El presidente ejecutivo prometió la salida del Grupo Orlegi en caso de que el conjunto rojiblanco no consiga el ascenso a Primera
articles.summary: El presidente ejecutivo prometió la salida del Grupo Orlegi en caso de que el conjunto rojiblanco no consiga el ascenso a Primera
articles.body: José Riestra ha sido el encargado de romper el silencio en el Sporting de Gijón tras la derrota en el derbi asturiano. Lo hizo en una entrevista concedida al podcast Arquitectos - LaLiga, en la que el presidente ejecutivo remarcó su convicción en lograr el ascenso a Primera división. Tal es la seguridad que existe por parte de la propiedad mexicana, que Riestra aseguró que el Grupo Orlegi abandonaría el club en caso de no ascender a la máxima categoría. Una promesa arriesgada. “Hicimos un compromiso hace un par de meses como grupo de que si no lográbamos el ascenso, nos íbamos nosotros” confesaba José Riestra, que ha insistido en numerosas ocasiones a lo largo de la temporada en la capacidad del Sporting de luchar por el ascenso a Primera. Un objetivo que la entidad asturiana persigue desde hace una década y que tan solo estuvo cerca de conseguir en una ocasión desde la llegada del Grupo Orlegi a Gijón, hace ya cinco campañas. El agridulce inicio no nubla el objetivo del Sporting. Superada la séptima jornada, y tras la derrota en el derbi asturiano, el equipo rojiblanco está en mitad de la clasificación, con 10 de los 18 puntos posibles, lejos del inicio esperado por el Grupo Orlegi. “Tenemos que tener esa paciencia para poder ver lo que Larcamón tiene. Estoy convencido de que nos va a ayudar”, aseguraba el presidente ejecutivo, que refuerza la apuesta por Nicolás Larcamón, el elegido por el Sporting para lograr el ansiado ascenso de categoría.

articles.title: Alemania aprueba la extradición a España del hijo de Al-Thani tras su detención
articles.standfirst: El Juzgado de Instrucción 14 de Málaga ya le espera a Rakan Al-Thani, hijo mayor del jeque
articles.summary: El Juzgado de Instrucción 14 de Málaga ya le espera
articles.body: Nuevo movimiento en el procedimiento judicial contra la familia Al-Thani. Un tribunal alemán ha dado luz verde a la extradición a España de Rakan Al-Thani, hijo mayor del jeque Abdullah Al-Thani, después de que fuera detenido el pasado mes de septiembre en el aeropuerto de Múnich cuando trataba de viajar a Doha. Su entrega pone ahora el caso en manos de la justicia española, que deberá decidir si queda en libertad o ingresa en prisión. Rakan será el Juzgado de Instrucción número 14 de Málaga el encargado de determinar la situación del detenido una vez llegue a España. El hijo mayor del jeque permanecía en una prisión de Baviera desde el 12 de septiembre, cuando las autoridades alemanas ejecutaron la Orden Europea de Detención y Entrega emitida por la justicia española. Ahora, su extradición supone un nuevo capítulo en el procedimiento abierto contra la familia Al-Thani, accionista mayoritaria del Málaga CF. La justicia española había ordenado el pasado mes de julio la búsqueda, detención e ingreso en prisión de Abdullah Al-Thani y sus tres hijos, Nasser, Nayef y Rakan, mediante una orden de ámbito europeo e internacional. Una medida que, tal y como informó en su momento Radio MARCA Málaga, llegó después de las dificultades de las autoridades para localizar a la familia. La jueza ya había advertido de que los Al-Thani no respondían a los correos electrónicos facilitados para las comunicaciones judiciales y que tampoco parecían residir en los domicilios que habían comunicado en Doha. Abdullah Al-Thani y sus tres hijos están investigados por presuntos delitos de apropiación indebida, administración desleal y blanqueo de capitales durante su etapa al frente del Málaga CF. Con la extradición de Rakan, el procedimiento podrá continuar en España con el primero de los cuatro miembros de la familia puesto a disposición de la justicia española.

articles.title: Dinamarca - Portugal en directo | Última hora de UEFA Nations League en vivo hoy
articles.summary: DESCANSO EN COPENHAGUE. Gana Portugal con los goles de Cancelo y Ramos. Empató de forma momentánea Damsgaard con un golazo. Superior el equipo de Jorg
articles.body:
Muy buenas tardes. En algo menos de dos horas y media ( 20.45 horas, DAZN ) dará comienzo en el Parken de Copenhague el Dinamarca- Portugal , correspondiente a la tercera jornada del grupo 4 de la Liga A de la UEFA Nations League . Un partido con mucha miga, tanto clasificatoriamente como, sobre todo, por ser el primer encuentro tras la marcha de Cristiano Ronaldo de la concentración portuguesa . Muchas miradas puestas en la actuación de los de Jorge Jesus y muchas ganas de un bando y de otro de 'sacar la guadaña'.

Dinamarca afronta el partido tras perder frente a Noruega (3-2) y vencer a Gales (2-0), mientras que los portugueses lideran el grupo tras ganar tanto a galeses (1-0) como a noruegos (1-2). En este último partido empezó a estallar el 'caso Cristiano', después de que CR7 no disputara ni un solo minuto pese a calentar gran parte del segundo tiempo.

El balance entre ambas selecciones es muy favorable para Portugal: se han medido en 18 ocasiones con 12 triunfos para los portugueses, dos empates y cuatro victorias para Dinamarca . La selección danesa es, tras Luxemburgo , el combinado al que más veces se ha medido Portugal.

Ambas selecciones se midieron en los cuartos de final de la última Nations League, en la que Portugal pasó en la prórroga. Dinamarca se impuso en la por 1-0 y Portugal forzó la prórroga con un gol de Trincao en el minuto 86 que suponía el 3-2. El propio Trincao y Gonçalo Ramos sentenciaron la eliminatoria en el tiempo extra para el 5-2 final.

Venga, que arrancamos un partidazo. Un partido que no terminará con el pitido final, ya que habrá que estar muy atento a lo que diga Jorge Jesus sobre el 'caso Cristiano' en la rueda de prensa posterior al partido.

articles.title: Man City not 'above the rules', says No 10 after backlash to Burnham remarks
articles.summary: The prime minister said he would be "really concerned" if the club's owners sell up after Premier League rule breaches.
articles.body:
Downing Street has said Manchester City are not "above the rules" after Andy Burnham was criticised for his comments about the club's breaches of Premier League financial rules.

The prime minister said on Wednesday he would be "really concerned" if the club's owners decide to sell up after City were found guilty by an independent commission of most of the 115 charges they faced.

His remarks were branded "completely out of touch" and "extraordinary" by the Tories and took many in the football community by surprise.

In a statement following the backlash, Downing Street said the PM had made clear "the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules".

In an attempt to clarify the PM's position, a No 10 spokesperson added: "He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.

"Wherever wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences."

Man City deny any wrongdoing and have until Friday to submit an appeal.

Sources told BBC Sport that City are expected to claim that key sponsorship deals were funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club's owners, as part of an appeal.

Among the independent panel's findings were that City arranged "sham contracts" with a number of commercial partners as part of a scheme to disguise secret funding of more than £830m.

The Premier League said City "systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade".

In an interview on Wednesday with the BBC's political editor Chris Mason, Burnham - who was mayor of Greater Manchester until June - said he was "not getting directly involved in the process", saying it must be undertaken independently by the Premier League.

He said the situation was "contested by Manchester City" and it would be "wrong" to "jump to a conclusion".

Asked if he was worried the club's owners since 2008 - led by Sheikh Mansour, a royal and the United Arab Emirates deputy prime minister - might sell up, Burnham said: "I would be really concerned to lose them.

"They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is.

"I can't intervene more in the process, it would be wrong for me to do that."

In response, the Tories accused Burnham of "publicly backing the owners even as the investigation continues" and questioned whether "political pressure" was being applied.

Man City to argue sponsorship deals came from Abu Dhabi government

Criminal investigation? Relegation or expulsion? The key Man City questions

The intricate web Man City spun to con the Premier League

Shadow minister for sport Louie French called for the government to "keep politics out of football and ensure the Premier League's independent commission can do its job free of outside influence".

"The club face unprecedented allegations and fans are horrified by what they are reading in the papers," the Tory MP said.

"Yet Burnham is publicly backing the owners even as the investigation continues. Fans will rightly ask whether political pressure is being applied here and how it relates to the owners' well-reported investments in Manchester.

"Football must be governed independently, with the rules applying equally to everyone. Fans deserve confidence that no club or owner is above those rules."

And Lib Dem MP Anna Sabine, the party's spokesperson on sport, said: "Fans of every club deserve to know the rules apply to everyone... Burnham needs to remember he's prime minister for everyone, not just Manchester."

It comes as the chairwoman of the Commons Treasury committee, Labour MP Dame Meg Hillier, wrote to HMRC on Thursday to ask for reassurance that it has "seized of the importance" of the case for any potential tax implications.

In his BBC interview, Burnham also said he was "of course" confident that his own interactions with City's owners as Greater Manchester mayor would stand up to scrutiny.

He compared City's situation to how the club he supports, Everton, had been charged with a more minor breach of Premier League financial rules in 2023, but said he "hold[s] the view very firmly that they weren't fairly treated in that process".

Burnham made his comments amid widespread shock in football about the scale of the independent commission's findings – and the strength of Premier League comments about City's actions.

The independent panel that found City guilty of rule breaches will hold a sanctions hearing – which could take months to convene – to decide the punishment, which could include a huge fine or points deduction.

City have maintained their innocence of all the accusations made.

The chairman of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) – set up by the government in 2025 – said the case had raised "serious issues".

In a statement, David Kogan said the IFR "has powers to assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives and we will use these powers where appropriate", while "taking account of the findings made by the Leagues".

He added that proceedings remain ongoing and he hoped for a quick resolution.

articles.title: Man City: HMRC urged to scrutinise tax implications of verdict revealed by Premier League
articles.summary: The Treasury Committee, which is responsible for overseeing HMRC, has urged the body to scrutinise tax implications of the Manchester City verdict.
articles.body:
Findings from the Premier League's case against Manchester City require scrutiny from His Majesty's Revenue and Customs, the chair of a cross-party group of MPs has told the tax authority.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that an independent commission found City guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

City have repeatedly denied guilt, and have signalled an intent to lodge an appeal by Friday.

The club were found to have artificially inflated revenue through "sham" sponsorship agreements with the help of their owners.

The independent commission which studied the case found City "utilised devices" to "disguise the true extent of certain club liabilities".

The Treasury Committee, which is responsible for overseeing policies and administration of HMRC, has therefore asked whether the government department has requested the redacted documents contained within the commission's report.

Dame Meg Hillier, chair of the Treasury Committee, said she would "welcome reassurance from HMRC that you are seized of the importance of these issues and the public interest in this case".

The letter follows a report from the Tax Policy Associates , external which claims City failed to pay as much as £12m in unpaid tax because of a "sham" contract with former manager Roberto Mancini.

In addition to unpaid income tax and National Insurance, the report claims City could face a penalty charge that would take their liabilities to £24m.

Man City not 'above the rules', says No 10 after backlash to Burnham remarks

City to argue sponsorship deals came from Abu Dhabi government

Manchester City will claim as part of their appeal that key sponsorship deals were funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club's owners.

Owners Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) - a private investment company belonging to United Arab Emirates vice-president and deputy prime minister Sheikh Mansour - are said to have topped up the value of commercial deals as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to the scale of £830.69m.

This, it was argued, enabled the club to appear to comply with Premier League and Uefa financial rules.

However, as first reported by the Daily Mail and Times, sources have told BBC Sport that City are expected to tell an appeal board that they have evidence showing the money directed to sponsors came from the Abu Dhabi government, rather than from ADUG.

Premier League rules allow state-owned bodies to sponsor clubs.

The independent commission detailed how City had "denied there had ever been any disguised funding scheme of the type alleged by the Premier League. Its case was that [it] had misunderstood how Abu Dhabi sponsorship agreements had been funded... The reality was [the club contested] that Abu Dhabi sponsors had always been liable for all recorded sponsorship fees and all had in fact been paid to the club by Abu Dhabi sponsors from their own funds/resources.

"No part of any recorded sponsorship fee had been paid by ADUG or from using ADUG funds. Abu Dhabi sponsors had from time to time applied for financial assistance from the Abu Dhabi government toward their liability to pay the recorded sponsorship fees - such applications had been granted…"

The independent commission rejected this submission as "untrue", saying: "We concluded that it was an 'explanation' that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to obscure and conceal the realities of the disguised funding scheme."

City's argument is likely to lead to renewed debate over the extent to which City's ownership is separate from the Abu Dhabi state, and over the ramifications of club ownership with state connections.

Mansour is a member of the ruling family of Abu Dhabi, and the brother of UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.

Since the takeover in 2008, City have insisted the club is a completely private enterprise, and not state-owned. However, some critics have questioned the distinction, with human rights campaigners claiming the ownership of City has been used to "sportswash" the UAE.

On Saturday, City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak referred to "irrefutable evidence" that he claimed supports the club's claims of innocence. City have claimed the commission's decision contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe".

It has emerged that Al Mubarak, who was appointed chairman of City following the takeover in 2008, is named as an Emirati diplomat on the UK government's current directory of all foreign representatives.

Representatives of foreign states and their diplomatic staff "enjoy privileges and immunities under the Diplomatic Privileges Act (1964)", giving diplomats immunity from prosecution under criminal, civil and administrative laws.

City's principal sponsor Etihad Airways has said it is considering legal action against the Premier League, claiming the release of the commission findings had "damaging implications… despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings".

The UAE's state-owned national airline said it "categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements".

Etihad is owned by sovereign wealth fund L'Imad which is chaired by the Crown Prince of Abu Dhabi, the son of the UAE president.

The Premier League declined to comment when contacted by BBC Sport.

articles.summary: Javier Muiños arropó al entrenador en Radio MARCA y Rafael Contreras ha defendido el nuevo proyecto, aunque todavía no conocen la victoria
articles.body: El Cádiz mantiene su confianza en Albert Celades pese a un inicio de temporada en el que el equipo todavía no ha conseguido ganar después de siete jornadas. Las intervenciones de Javier Muiños y Rafael Contreras de las últimas horas reflejan el respaldo al proyecto y una petición de paciencia, con la mejoría del conjunto amarillo como argumento para confiar en una reacción. Muiños, codirector de fútbol, fue especialmente explícito durante su participación del miércoles en la Tertulia Amarilla de Radio MARCA Provincia de Cádiz, desde el restaurante La Bodega. "Estamos con Celades y le transmitimos tranquilidad", aseguró. El responsable deportivo recordó que el entrenador llegó sin pretemporada, aunque reconoció la urgencia de sumar triunfos. "Necesitamos ganar", admitió, antes de explicar que dentro del club perciben avances: "Vemos que el equipo cada día está más cerca, el trabajo está ahí". Este jueves también el vicepresidente Rafael Contreras reforzó la defensa del proyecto tras la tradicional ofrenda floral del equipo. Sin referirse expresamente al entrenador, pidió mantener la confianza en el rumbo elegido. "Todos queremos que el Cádiz gane. Estamos trabajando para revertir ese desencanto y tenemos que mantener la paciencia", manifestó. Contreras destacó que el cambio ha sido profundo tanto en la plantilla como en el estilo y el modelo deportivo. Además, cifró la inversión en jugadores en más de 12 millones de euros y aseguró que existe una gestión y un liderazgo claramente definidos. El respaldo a Celades convive, por tanto, con la necesidad de resultados. La dirección deportiva entiende que el equipo está más cerca de ganar, mientras la vicepresidencia defiende la apuesta realizada y agradece el apoyo de una afición que sigue esperando la primera victoria. La próxima oportunidad será este sábado contra el Leganés, precisamente el último equipo al que le ganó el Cádiz.

articles.standfirst: Nació Oriana: el motivo personal por el que Gustavo Puerta dejó la Selección Colombia
articles.summary: Nació Oriana: el motivo personal por el que Gustavo Puerta dejó la Selección Colombia
articles.body: El centrocampista colombiano Gustavo Puerta vive uno de los momentos más especiales de su vida personal. En plena concentración con la Selección Colombia de cara a la gira de amistosos de preparación, el mediocampista de 22 años recibió un permiso especial por parte del cuerpo técnico encabezado por Néstor Lorenzo para ausentarse temporalmente y viajar a estar presente en el nacimiento de su primera hija. La pequeña, nombrada Oriana, nació el lunes 28 de septiembre de 2026 en la Fundación San José de Buga (Valle del Cauca). La noticia fue compartida por el propio futbolista del Olympiacos y su esposa, la empresaria y creadora de contenido Valeria Valencia, a través de emotivas fotografías en redes sociales donde se les ve cargando a la recién nacida en sus primeras horas de vida. "Septiembre: el mes en el que dejé de imaginar cómo eras y por fin te sostuve entre mis brazos", expresó el volante colombiano en una amorosa publicación. La pareja, que contrajo matrimonio en marzo de 2026 en España, recibió miles de mensajes de felicitación por parte de compañeros de la Selección Colombia, colegas del fútbol internacional y fanáticos. A raíz de este evento familiar, Puerta debió ausentarse momentáneamente de la dinámica del equipo nacional. Sin embargo, tras acompañar a su esposa e hija durante el parto y los primeros cuidados, el mediocampista reordenó su itinerario para reincorporarse de inmediato a la concentración de Colombia en Estados Unidos. El volante ya se encuentra a disposición del cuerpo técnico para el encuentro de fecha FIFA, reafirmando su compromiso tanto en el ámbito personal como profesional en este nuevo ciclo con la Selección absoluta.

articles.title: Croatia vs England: Why is Nations League match being played behind closed doors?
articles.summary: BBC Sport's Ask Me Anything team explains why England's Nations League match in Croatia is being played in front of a reduced capacity.
articles.body:
England's match against Croatia in the Nations League on Saturday will be played behind closed doors in Rijeka.

The game will take place in front of a reduced crowd in the same venue in which the two sides met, also behind closed doors, in a 0-0 draw in October 2018.

The limited capacity is because of crowd disturbances involving Croatia fans during a Nations League match against France in March 2025.

Seven fans were taken into custody on suspicion of making Nazi salutes during the match, and released without prosecution because of a lack of evidence.

In their section of Stade de France, where that match took place, Croatia supporters also set off fireworks.

On top of that, Croatia were also prohibited from having travelling supporters in their 2-1 win in the Czech Republic last Saturday.

While the match is officially being played behind closed doors, there will be some supporters in attendance.

Between 3,000 and 6,000 Croatian schoolchildren have been permitted to attend the match at Stadion Riejka.

Initially, England fans were not allowed to attend. Following discussions with Uefa and England, the Three Lions were later permitted to have 100 complimentary tickets given to their fans.

articles.title: Man City charges: Treasury Committee writes to HMRC to ask about tax implications of Premier League investigation
articles.summary: Man City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City deny all charges and have confirmed they will appeal against the ruling and have until Friday to do so
articles.body:
HMRC could investigate whether City paid the right amount of tax and national insurance during the nine seasons they have been found guilty of financial rule breaches.

In the letter, Dame Meg Hillier MP asks JP Marks, permanent secretary of HMRC, whether the department has received an unredacted version of the Premier League's report and requests "reassurance from HMRC that you are seized of the importance of these issues and the public interest in the case".

Hillier also says she would welcome an "overview of current HMRC work around football clubs."

The letter reads: "I would be interested in any common issues around taxation (including the taxation of remuneration) that you have found in their practices and how HMRC is tackling them."

The deadline for a reply is set at Thursday October 15.

Man City continue to deny wrongdoing and plan to launch an appeal against the verdict, which they must do by Friday.

The Premier League investigation into City was triggered by the publication of hacked internal emails in the German magazine Der Spiegel in 2018.

Der Spiegel said it had evidence which appeared to show that Roberto Mancini, who was City manager from 2009 to 2013, had a secret second contract.

As well as being paid £1.45m net by City, a company connected to him in Italy was being paid £1.75m for a four-day annual coaching consultancy commitment at Abu Dhabi-based UAE Pro League club Al Jazira.

Analysis: What are the tax implications of Man City's guilty judgement?

"The Treasury Committee have written to HMRC to ask about the tax implications of the Premier League's investigation into Manchester City.

"For instance, HMRC could investigate to see if City have been paying the right amount of tax over the nine seasons when they have been found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules.

"The investigation into Manchester City was triggered by some hacked internal emails which were published by Der Speigel in 2018.

"According to Der Speigel , some of those emails appeared to show that former manager Roberto Mancini had two contracts. One for managing Manchester City, for which he was paid £1.45m, and a second contract whereby £1.75m was being paid per year to a company associated with him.

"I perhaps think what the Treasury Committe are getting at is just making sure that HMRC is going to be looking into this. Potentially, is this a case where the right amount of tax and national insurance wasn't paid?

"The Treasury Committee also ask [in their letter] for reassurances that the department has seized the importance of the case."

articles.title: Pat McAfee Slams Critics After On-Air Jason Kelce Incident: ‘I Hope You All Rot’
articles.summary: Pat McAfee is addressing his haters after he called out Jason Kelce for a slip of the tongue earlier this week on ESPN. Kelce, 38, appeared as usual on ESPN’...
articles.body:
Pat McAfee is addressing his haters after he called out Jason Kelce for a slip of the tongue earlier this week on ESPN.

Kelce, 38, appeared as usual on ESPN's Monday Night Football broadcast between the Philadelphia Eagles and Chicago Bears on Monday, September 28, alongside cohosts Scott Van Pelt and McAfee. During halftime, the former Eagles center repeatedly referred to his old team by saying "we," prompting McAfee, 39, to joke, "A lot of 'we' talk out of Jason for Philly."

Kelce then apologized, saying, "Sorry, sorry, I forget. Sorry, Bears fans."

On the Wednesday, September 30 episode of his live ESPN and YouTube show , the former Indianapolis Colts punter took a moment to first address some of the criticism he received for that incident.

"Now, I usually mind my own, but if you thought I was being serious whenever I pointed out that Jason Kelce was saying 'we' about the Philadelphia Eagles, knowing who Jason Kelce is, with the Philadelphia Eagles at the Monday Night Football halftime, you have no brain, and I think you should just realize that," he shared.

McAfee's comment seemed to reference former ESPN analyst Ryan Clark , who took to X the day after the game to post, "I'm trying to mind my own, but hell yea it's 'We' Future Hall of Famer!"

Clark, 46, added, "You're a legend @JasonKelce. Blood, sweat, tears, & glory in Philly. No one can take that away. You can still do your job the right way! Bump anyone saying differently."

Many in the analyst's replies took his post as a dig at McAfee.

"I don't love just the lying and the stuff that happens on my name these days," McAfee himself added on Wednesday's show, not mentioning anyone by name.

"But just saying stuff to continue to add gas to a flame that isn't real when you're in this place and carry as much weight as you definitely do, I think it's a little bit of a piling on," he said, before concluding, "and I hope you all rot. All of you."

Clark has not responded to McAfee's latest comments.

Kelce, meanwhile, appears to have taken the on-air callout in stride — with his New Heights podcast even poking fun at the moment by reposting the clip on X , along with a Fresh Prince of Bel-Air meme.

articles.title: Atlético boosts governance to support the club's digital transformation
articles.summary: Digital transformation has expanded football clubs’ scope of activity far beyond the four lines of the pitch. Initiatives related to the fan experience and r...
articles.body:
Digital transformation has expanded football clubs' scope of activity far beyond the four lines of the pitch. Initiatives related to the fan experience and relationship programs through the Club's digital platforms have come to require not only investment in technology, but also increasing attention to regulatory and governance aspects.

In recent years, Atlético has carried out a series of projects that reflect this evolution. From expanding digital services for the Massa Atleticana to initiatives linked to the Galo Museum and the Atlético Memory Center, the Club has been structuring processes so that these actions are developed in line with legal requirements and management best practices.

This work has gained even greater relevance in light of the regulatory changes affecting the sports sector. The entry into force of the General Sports Law (Law No. 14,597/2023), the consolidation of the General Personal Data Protection Law – LGPD (Law No. 13,709/2018), and the progress of discussions related to the protection of children and adolescents in the digital environment have increased the need for sports organizations to monitor these issues on an ongoing basis.

In this context, Atlético has been improving its internal workflows so that issues related to data protection, risk management, and compliance are taken into account from the early planning stages of new projects.

This work is supported by specialized regulatory analysis focused on identifying the impacts that new laws, regulations, and interpretations by oversight bodies/entities may have on the Club's initiatives. The goal is to translate regulatory changes into practical guidelines for decision-making, allowing strategic projects to be developed with greater legal certainty, predictability, and alignment with governance best practices.

All of this work is backed by the technical support of the specialized consultancy of Pironti+Moura Advogados Associados, which assists the Club in analyzing new regulatory frameworks and building governance mechanisms aimed at ensuring the legal security of the initiatives under development.

More than simply meeting legal requirements, the goal is to ensure that innovation moves forward in an integrated manner with risk management and compliance, allowing Galo to continue developing projects focused on the experience of the Massa and the modernization of its operations.

By continuously strengthening its governance structure, the Club reinforces its commitment to responsible management, prepared to keep pace with the transformations in football and the challenges of an increasingly digital environment.

articles.title: Former Barcelona star wants to return to the club as a free agent next summer
articles.summary: A former member of the attacking ranks at La Liga champions Barcelona is eyeing a return to Catalunya’s capital in the summer of 2027.That’s according to Dia...
articles.body:
A former member of the attacking ranks at La Liga champions Barcelona is eyeing a return to Catalunya's capital in the summer of 2027.

That's according to Diario Sport, who point to João Félix as the player in question.

Frontman Félix for his part spent the duration of the 2023/24 campaign plying his trade in Barcelona colours, on loan from La Liga rivals Atlético Madrid .

The Portuguese showcased flashes of his unquestionable quality over the course of his 12 months in Blaugrana , but, as has proven the case throughout his career, ultimately lacked the consistency required to convince the Camp Nou brass to make his signing permanent.

Félix has since bounced around several clubs, most recently landing in Saudi Arabia with Al-Nassr in 2025. And his time in the Middle East, to date, has proven a major success.

Félix was named Player of the Year in the SPL last time out, after Al-Nassr finally did enough to secure the league title. He has also reestablished himself as an important figure with the Portuguese national team.

And if the latest word stemming from the Spanish media is anything to go by, then the 26-year-old is evidently keen to make use of this momentum to secure for himself a fresh chance at one of world football's leading clubs.

'Félix is clear that he is going to return to European football. His big dream is to return to Barça on a free transfer. His agent, Jorge Mendes, has already communicated it to the Blaugrana club for next summer.'

It now remains to be seen whether or not the interest of the Spanish champions in a reunion with the gifted but frustrating frontman is mutual…

articles.title: Liverpool Are Hoping To Sign This Ligue 1 Midfielder: Should Iraola Bring Him To Anfield Again?
articles.summary: In a recent report, journalist Pete O’Rourke claimed that Liverpool are hoping to re-sign Olympique Lyonnais midfielder Tyler Morton. It has been mentioned t...
articles.body:
In a recent report , journalist Pete O'Rourke claimed that Liverpool are hoping to re-sign Olympique Lyonnais midfielder Tyler Morton . It has been mentioned that the Reds are keeping tabs on the progress of the English talent as they look to bring him back to Anfield next year.

Morton's Impressive Form In French Football

Morton has made a solid start to his Lyon career as he has put in a string of impressive displays for them in the middle of the park. The 23-year-old has scored one goal in ten matches for the French club this season across all fronts.

The English talent is currently among the most talented central midfielders in Ligue 1 . Hence, it is no surprise that the Reds are showing interest in re-signing him next year.

His current contract at the French club will run out in the summer of 2030, which could make it tough for Liverpool to land him on a cut-price deal this winter or at the end of this season.

LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 16: Tyler Morton of Liverpool trains during the UEFA Champions League 2024/25 League Phase MD1 Training Session at AXA Melwood Training Centre on September 16, 2024 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Lewis Storey/Getty Images)

Should Liverpool Boss Andoni Iraola Bring Morton Back?

Morton loves a tackle and can time his challenges well to make some important interceptions for his team inside his half. He usually clears the danger when the opposition are on the front foot and is a tidy passer as well from midfield.

The English talent can even chip in by scoring the odd goal for his side. Morton is primarily a defensive midfielder but can also operate as a box-to-box midfielder if asked to do so. He already knows the Merseyside club well from his previous spell with them and won't take any time to adjust to life in England.

We can expect Morton to add more quality and depth to Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola's midfield. He has what it takes to fight for a regular first-team spot at Anfield in the coming years.

At 23, Morton has his peak years ahead of him, which makes him a decent choice for the Reds to consider in 2027. He will also help the Merseyside giants compete across all fronts over the next few seasons. Therefore, Iraola should focus on going all out to bring him back to Anfield in the January transfer window or at the end of this campaign.

articles.title: Alex Golesh won't preach 'patience' for Auburn football — even if Charles Barkley will
articles.summary: Charles Barkley thinks Auburn football fans should be patient with first-year head coach Alex Golesh in the fold. Golesh? He doesn't see it that way.
articles.body:
AUBURN — He was appreciative of the kind words, Sir Charles, but he didn't quite see eye to eye.

Auburn football head coach Alex Golesh expressed his thanks for Charles Barkley 's support on Auburn 's Tiger Talk coaches radio show Wednesday, Sept. 30, specifically addressing recent comments from the noted Auburn alumnus by way of an audience question.

"He (Barkley) recently said, 'Hey, Auburn nation, let's be patience, all right?'" Andy, among the show's viewing public at Baumhower's Victory Grille, said. "I can't say exactly what he said, because the FCC is probably monitoring this."

Barkley shared those sentiments ahead of the annual Bruce and Barkley golf event Monday. In specific, he said: "You Auburn people are so damn impatient — and y'all always compare yourself to Tuscaloosa, which is stupid. I'm very happy with our football coach. People who know football tell me we got us a winner, that if we can just be patient and give him an opportunity to put his footprint on it. ... Guys have no patience anymore and that's unfortunate, but I got patience with him, and I'm excited for him."

Golesh's view of the matter — particularly, the word "patience" — wasn't so similar.

"I don't know if I've ever used that word with anybody," Golesh said. "There's things that you can't shortcut, and that's the building of a culture, the building of a standard. Expectations, like that stuff takes time, but the expectation is you win now. I'm fully aware of the job that I took, and the fact that there's an expectation and a standard. It's got to match the investment, which is why we made the decision to come here, because I do think that the investment matches the expectation."

Through four games, Auburn is 3-1 overall under Golesh and 1-1 against the SEC, suffering its only loss to No. 8 Florida . The road ahead appears packed with Florida equivalents, as Auburn will face five ranked opponents and play four road games in its next six contests.

Regardless of the results, Golesh doesn't appear keen to preach patience, at least in the scope of results, any time soon.

"I don't know that I would ever say that," Golesh said. "You can't look at a room full of competitors, in terms of our staff and our players and say, 'Man, everybody just chill out here. It's going to take a little bit of time.' ... Our job is truly to be as good as we can as fast as we can. I appreciate Sir Charles for preaching that, but at the end of the day, we've got to go win football games as fast as we can."

articles.title: Lionel Messi: Inter Miami's former Barcelona superstar buys second Spanish club, CD Eldense
articles.summary: Argentine football great Lionel Messi becomes the owner of Spanish second division club CD Eldense.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi has completed his purchase of Spanish second division club CD Eldense.

The deal is subject to regulatory approval and is the second Spanish club that Argentina great Messi has invested in, with the 39-year-old having bought Catalan side Cornella in April.

"Club Deportivo Eldense officially announces the acquisition of the club by Leo Messi, marking the start of a new and exciting chapter in the club's history, which spans more than 100 years," CD Eldense stated on their website. , external

CD Eldense are 19th in the 22-team Spanish second division with one win and five points from their opening seven games.

Former Barcelona forward Messi, who won the 2022 World Cup with Argentina, plays for American club Inter Miami in Major League Soccer and announced his retirement from international football in August.

An eight-time Ballon d'Or winner, he reached a "preliminary agreement" to become CD Eldense's majority shareholder in September, with the process now complete.

"The arrival of one of the most important figures in the history of sport as owner of CD Eldense marks the beginning of a long-term project aimed at promoting the club's sporting, institutional, and social development," added the Alicante-based club.

Messi left Argentina for Spain when he was 13 and made his first-team debut for Barcelona aged 17 in October 2004.

He went on to score a record 672 goals in 778 games before leaving for French club Paris St-Germain in 2021, prior to joining Inter Miami in the United States in 2023.

Messi's former Real Madrid rival Cristiano Ronaldo, who plays for Saudi Pro League side Al-Nassr, bought a 25% stake in Spanish side Almeria in February.
